segments.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: בַּכֹּל כּוּ׳. בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: בַּמֶּה שֶׁהוּא מַדִּירוֹ, וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אַף בְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ מַדִּירוֹ. כֵּיצַד? אָמַר לוֹ: ״קֻוֽנָּם אִשְׁתִּי נֶהֱנֵית לִי״, וְאָמַר ״קֻוֽנָּם אִשְׁתִּי וּבָנַי נֶהֱנִין לִי״. בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אִשְׁתּוֹ מוּתֶּרֶת וּבָנָיו אֲסוּרִין, וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ מוּתָּרִין.
segments.en: § The mishna states: «Beit Shammai say» that they may take a vow in such a case «using every» means of vowing except for an oath, while Beit Hillel say they may take a vow even using an oath. «Beit Shammai say:» One may vow only «about that which» the extortionist «compels him to take a vow» but may not add to it. «And Beit Hillel say:» One may take a vow «even about that which he does not compel him to take a vow. How» so? If the extortionist «said to him» that he should «say: Benefiting from me is konam for my wife» if the vow is not true, «and he said: Benefiting from me is konam for my wife and my children, Beit Shammai say: His wife is permitted» to benefit from him, since the extortionist demanded that he take that vow, «but his children,» whom he added of his own accord, «are prohibited» from benefiting from their father. «And Beit Hillel say: Both these and those are permitted» to benefit from him.
